Chapter Three: Loyalty and Doubt—How Trust Is Built in a World of Fear
In the intelligence world, nothing is left to chance. Every relationship, every word, every single action—it's all under constant scrutiny. Loyalty isn’t just a slogan here; it’s a basic requirement for survival.
But real loyalty? That’s rare. Most of the time, it’s either forced by fear or driven by personal gain.
From day one, everyone learns that suspicion is the default. Imagine this: during a regular team meeting, someone is suddenly asked to write a report about the coworker sitting right next to them. There’s no obvious reason. It’s just a test of loyalty. At first, the person feels uneasy—who wouldn’t? But pretty quickly, it sinks in: refusing might be seen as a lack of trust. So, they go along with it, write the report... but can’t shake the feeling that they’ve betrayed a colleague, even if it’s “just part of the job.”
Loyalty in this world is built on shaky ground. Sometimes it’s family ties or shared interests. Other times, it’s pushed through intimidation or outright threats. Take, for example, a junior officer whose family is well known for supporting the regime. That family connection gives him some temporary protection, sure—but it also turns him into a target for suspicion. Every move he makes is watched closely, and even the smallest slip can be seen as betrayal.
And betrayal isn’t always obvious, or even intentional. Sometimes, being late to an important meeting or avoiding a sensitive topic is all it takes to spark doubt. One day, an employee notices their boss suddenly acting cold. At first, they’re confused. Later, they find out a report was written accusing them of not being enthusiastic enough about their work. The report isn’t based on facts—just impressions and suspicions. In that moment, it hits them: your fate here can really hinge on a single word or the tiniest action.
In this atmosphere, everyone gets caught in a web of suspicion. Not even family is safe. Picture this: late at night, an officer sits with his younger brother, talking about the future. He suddenly realizes his brother’s become guarded, like there’s an invisible wall between them. That wall of doubt isn’t just at work—it creeps into every corner of their lives.
Over time, everyone figures out what it takes to survive: hide your feelings, pretend to be loyal, and never, ever give anyone a reason to doubt you. One day, someone watches as a coworker is called in for questioning—just because of a normal phone call with a relative overseas. There’s no real evidence of anything, but just making the call is enough to set off alarms. In that moment, it becomes crystal clear: everyone’s at risk, and loyalty alone isn’t enough to keep you safe.
And yet, in the middle of all this, some people try to hold onto their principles. There was a story about an employee who refused to frame an innocent person, even though the pressure was huge. He paid a steep price for it, but deep down, he knew he’d managed to hold onto a piece of his dignity. Those moments are rare, but they remind everyone that—even in the toughest circumstances—people still have choices.
So, what’s the key takeaway? In the world of intelligence, trust is a rare commodity, and real loyalty can’t be bought or forced. Everyone’s living in a circle of doubt, just trying to get through each day, searching for even a single honest moment in a world that’s full of suspicion.
